title: A learned stemness index guides a signature associated with breast-cancer outcomes
summary: Researchers used a pre-existing one-class logistic-regression stemness index to derive a breast-cancer expression signature. Higher positive-signature expression was associated with shorter relapse-free survival and with recorded five-year metastasis in a separate cohort. These are observational associations, not proof of a causal stem-cell mechanism.

evidence.tested: Expression from 1,247 TCGA records was correlated with the learned index to define positive and negative signatures. Outcome analyses used 2,032 relapse-free-survival records and 1,979 METABRIC records.
evidence.unknown: Existing learned index reused; signatures and cohorts may overlap, and no new independent risk-model accuracy or causal effect is claimed. Experimental mechanisms and compound results elsewhere in the paper are outside this record.
evidence.ai_role: A previously trained one-class logistic-regression index supplies the stemness representation used to select the outcome-associated signature.

source_review.scope: Exact primary front metadata and computational signature, bioinformatics and nonactionable clinical-association Results; operational experimental sections excluded.
